newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: French and Ivorian entrepreneurs meet.
newsitem.headline: French and Ivorian entrepreneurs meet.

text.p: Ivory Coast's prime minister opened a meeting of French and Ivorian business leaders on Tuesday, saying economic liberalisation had made the West African nation more investor friendly.
But some of those attending said the government should do more, particularly to help small companies wanting to invest in the world's top cocoa producer.
Prime Minister Daniel Kablan Duncan said the two-day workshop was designed to bring French and Ivorian entrepreneurs together and explain the new investment environment in Ivory Coast.
"It will first provide our partners with sufficient information on the recent development of the investing environment in the Ivory Coast, and then on the business opportunities generated," he said.
Duncan listed changes in investment and mining codes, liberalisation of labour laws and tax rates.
Some French delegates said the prospects were encouraging thanks to political and social stability in Ivory Coast but others felt more needed to be done.
"We are in a relatively simple judicial environnment," Jean-Pierre Journee, a French fiscal consultant, said, but he added: "Taxes are too heavy for small companies."
About 250 companies from textile, services, agriculture, industry, mining, public works, technology and energy sectors were attending the meeting.
